chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! Beware of chewing gum, for I chewed gum today while I was fasting, and I found something from it in myself.'

key_terms.عِلْكاً: Gum (specifically a type of chewing gum or resin)
key_terms.نَفْسِي: Self/soul (here referring to one's internal state or essence)

ai.seo_question: Does chewing gum break the fast according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) advises against chewing gum (*ilk*) while fasting, citing a personal experience where he felt a distinct internal change or distraction after doing so. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *khulus* (purity of focus) and spiritual mindfulness during fasting, suggesting that actions which divert the heart or alter one's spiritual state, even if they do not physically break the fast, are discouraged to preserve the fast's deeper essence.
